title: crumb: how does a running state-mode session autosave its cookies to the vault?
scope: Timer-driven saves in one running state-mode supervisor: snapshot Chrome, merge with the latest vault entry, rewrite it.
omissions: Launch, run handle files, and crumb sync/close signal saves
Profile mode, agent CDP use, login/import/capture/check flows

groups.label: Local machine
groups.description: Local self-managed host, same OS user

nodes.label: Supervisor
nodes.description: Chrome owner; best-effort saves, no file lock

nodes.label: Chrome
nodes.description: Owned child on temp profile; exit skips save

notes.title: Timer, errors and exit
notes.text: Default 30s (--autosave 0 = no timer). Ticks join an in-flight save; unchanged snapshots skip. Errors only logged. Chrome self-close exits with no final save; SIGTERM/SIGINT save first.

notes.title: Three-way merge, no lock
notes.text: Each save re-reads the entry, applies only before→after changes, adds provenance + browser hints, then writes a temp file and renames it. No lock: writes between read and rename are lost.

notes.title: Vault key custody
notes.text: Key from CRUMB_KEY, else config.json's store: macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service or ~/.crumb/key (0600); cached per process. Session is AES-256-GCM (id as AAD); header is plaintext.
